The ritual

Coffee that tastes like home.

Northside Coffee Co. is a Latin-American coffee shop with character to spare — soaring oak walls, brass light, a Talavera-tile counter, and a wall that rotates through the work of local artists.

The house specialty is café de olla: coffee brewed slowly with cinnamon, spice and piloncillo, the way it's made at home in Mexico. From there the menu runs deep — horchata with churros, Tía Rosa with mazapán and oat milk, an Abuelita chocoflan, beans roasted in Veracruz.

It's made to order and worth the minute it takes. Come for a drink and stay a while — for a Día de Muertos ofrenda, a still-life workshop, or just a quiet corner with the big picture window onto the Westside.

The space

Folk art, marigolds, and a whole lot of character.

Oak paneling, Mexican folk paintings, a Día de Muertos ofrenda, and a rotating wall of local artists. Small inside, with a patio out front when the weather's right.

Do you take reservations?
No reservations needed — Ollama is walk-in. Drop by, order at the counter, and grab a seat inside or out on the patio.
What's a coffee flight?
Pick any two drinks from the menu and we serve them side by side on a branded paddle — the easiest way to taste a few before you find your favorite.
Where do I park?
Free street parking runs along Main St. It can fill up at peak times, so it's an easy one to pair with a walk around the Westside.
Are the drinks made to order?
Every drink is made by hand, so it can take a few minutes when we're busy — there's room to wait, and it's worth it.
